claim: New clean power more than met the growth in demand across China last year, leading to a small decline in coal output, according to think tank Ember.
label: TRUE
annotatorNote: [AI label: Claude, 2026-10-05 - not yet checked by the human annotator] Ember (8 Sep 2026): clean electricity met all of China's additional power demand in 2025 (demand +5%), pushing thermal generation down 0.7%, most of it coal - the first fall since 2015. 'Coal output' read as coal-fired generation, which is what Ember measures; 'small decline' fits 0.7%.
